# statart

<!-- badges: start -->

[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental) [![CRAN status](https://www.r-pkg.org/badges/version/statart)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=statart)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/socimh/statart/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/socimh/statart/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)

<!-- badges: end -->

[statart](https://socimh.github.io/statart/) is a set of functions that combines Stata-inspired features with tidyverse-style operations.

The package focuses on exploring and preparing data:

- `tab()`, `tab1()`, and `tab2()` for frequency tables.
- `fre()`, `fre1()`, and `fre2()` for frequency tables with totals.
- `summ()` and `tabstat()` for summary statistics.
- `codebook()` and `variables()` for variable inspection.
- `s_select()`, row calculations, conversion helpers, and binning for data preparation.

The `0.2.0.9000` development series retires the import/export, regression-table,
and detailed-codebook wrappers in preparation for `0.3.0`. See the
[migration guide](MIGRATION.md) for direct package alternatives and breaking
changes. This experimental package is undergoing stabilization; see
[DEVELOPMENT.md](DEVELOPMENT.md) for the verified status and remaining work.

## Installation

You can install the development version of statart like so:

```r
devtools::install_github("socimh/statart")
```

R 4.1.0 or later and a suitable build toolchain are required to install from
source. Rich table formatting is optional and requires `flextable`.

## Example

### Load the package

Load `statart` and the data-manipulation package used in these examples.

```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(statart)
library(dplyr)
```

### codebook()

View the codebook of `lifeexp`.

```{r}
codebook(lifeexp)
```

### summ()

Summarise selected numeric variables in `mtcars`.

```{r}
summ(mtcars, mpg, wt)
```

Choose numeric variables deliberately: means and standard deviations of factor
codes may have no substantive interpretation.

### tab()

Tabulate a single variable:

```{r}
tab(starwars, sex)
```

`tab1()` tabulates variables one by one as a list, and `s_match()` can select variables in a Stata style.


```{r}
tab1(starwars, s_match("*color"))
```

`tab2()` cross-tabulates two variables.

```{r}
tab2(starwars, sex, gender)
```


### fre()

`fre()` family functions simply add total rows (and total columns in `fre2()`) to their `tab()` counterparts.

`fre()` and `fre2()` return tibbles by default. `fre1()` returns a list of tibbles.

```{r}
fre(starwars, sex)
```

For optional rich formatting, install `flextable` and request it explicitly:

```r
fre(starwars, sex, .type = "flextable")
```

### Row calculations and binning

Row helpers return vectors that can be used in `mutate()`:

```{r}
tibble(a = c(1, NA, 3), b = c(3, NA, 5)) |>
  mutate(row_average = row_mean(a, b))
```

`cut_quantile()` keeps equal values in the same group. Ties can reduce the number
of intervals, with a warning, rather than splitting equal values by row order.
